title: The Glass Passage
story:
The sky over Oakhaven darkened with the sudden, dramatic speed of the highland rainy season. James felt the shift in the wind first—a cool, damp gust that smelled of wet stone and distant pines, vividly reminding him of afternoons in the Great Canopy when the sky would split open. Around him, the bustling market square transformed into a flurry of motion. Vendors scrambled to pull heavy canvas tarps over their vegetable crates, and shoppers hurried under the deep eaves of the stone buildings.

He saw a merchant struggling to cover a stack of bright woolen blankets. He saw a child running with a flat basket of bread held high over her head. He saw a stray dog ducking beneath the dry shelter of a heavy wooden cart. Realizing his own fur would soon be thoroughly soaked, James secured his leather strap and darted across the slick cobblestones. Just as the first heavy droplets began to shatter against the pavement, he slipped through a grand stone archway into the safety of the Glass Passage.

Inside, the world became instantly dry and beautifully echoing. High above, a vaulted ceiling of iron frameworks and green-tinted glass panes caught the drumming rhythm of the downpour, diffusing the afternoon light into a soft, emerald glow that felt remarkably like the understory of his forest home. Along the sides of the passage, quiet shops displayed brass instruments, old books, and hand-woven textiles. James shook the water from his ears, climbed onto a dry stone bench, and watched the sheets of rain slide down the grand glass roof.

Nearby, a weaver named Mateo sat on a low wooden stool, calmly continuing his work on a backstrap loom anchored to a heavy iron pillar. Mateo's fingers moved with a quiet, hypnotic rhythm, passing vibrant red, yellow, and indigo threads through the warp. He did not shoo James away; instead, he offered a warm, crinkly-eyed smile and slid a small, leftover bundle of beautifully dyed cotton threads toward the edge of his workbench. James reached out, felt the rough warmth of the cotton, and carefully tucked the colorful threads into his canister alongside his remaining coin.
